projects.title: AnTix
projects.shortDescription: A Cloudflare-native ticketing and event-operations platform for selling, delivering, and validating QR tickets.
projects.description: AnTix is an end-to-end ticketing platform built for the operational reality of live events. It supports purchase through check-in with organizer administration, QR ticket delivery, and attendance workflows designed to keep payment, fulfillment, and entry state consistent under real traffic.
highlights: Used by 2 organizers across 5 live events to sell and validate 500 tickets
Verified Stripe webhooks with idempotent order and ticket creation
Automated QR delivery, resend, and partial-ticket recovery workflows
Mobile check-in safeguards against duplicate scans and inconsistent entry state
Reported 99% ticket-delivery rate supported by delivery logging and recovery tooling

sections.heading: What I Built
sections.body: I built the public purchasing experience, organizer workflows, backend APIs, and live-event check-in flow. The platform uses role-scoped authentication and D1 migrations to manage events, orders, tickets, user state, QR validation, and attendance.

sections.heading: Reliability at Checkout
sections.body: Stripe Checkout is paired with verified webhooks, reservations, verification logic, and duplicate-webhook handling so retries and network failures do not create duplicate fulfillment or an inconsistent payment state. Resend workflows log delivery attempts and provide recovery paths when tickets need to be resent.

sections.heading: Operational Lessons
sections.body: Production work centered on the awkward edges of live operations: email delivery, asynchronous processing, timeouts, and reliable deployment during active events. The result is a system built around recovery and observability, not just a successful happy path.

projects.title: FlexPOS
projects.shortDescription: A production desktop POS and inventory system that connects retail payment rules with barcode and receipt-printer workflows.
projects.description: FlexPOS centralizes checkout, inventory, transaction history, receipt printing, and operator workflows for two convenience stores. It was built around the practical details that generic prototypes skip: payment prioritization, item-level EBT eligibility, card-fee automation, hardware interruptions, and fast staff onboarding.
highlights: Deployed across 2 convenience stores with inventory and transaction support for 500+ SKUs
Supports cash, card, split-payment, card-fee, and item-level EBT eligibility rules
Approximately 50% faster checkout than manual price entry
Approximately 80% fewer card-fee errors through automated handling
Searchable transaction logs cut issue-resolution time by approximately 50%

sections.heading: Role & Build
sections.body: I designed, built, deployed, and actively maintained the desktop application in Python with a customizable CustomTkinter interface and SQLite-backed inventory and transaction processing. Store feedback directly informed iterative feature work and operator-focused refinements.

sections.heading: Checkout & Hardware
sections.body: The checkout engine calculates totals while applying payment, fee, and eligibility rules correctly. UPC barcode scanners and receipt printers are integrated into the workflow, with safeguards for device, communication, and interrupted-hardware failures to reduce transaction disruption.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.body: By replacing manual price entry with barcode-driven workflows and automating error-prone payment calculations, FlexPOS improved checkout speed and reduced card-fee mistakes in active store operations.

projects.title: Tranquility Task Tracker
projects.shortDescription: A mobile-first task and habit tracker for routines, recurring work, goals, and weekly reflection.
projects.description: Tranquility is an end-to-end productivity application focused on the repeatable work behind daily routines. It combines task and habit tracking with reminders, goals, weekly reviews, progress calculations, and a point-based motivation loop in a deliberately simple dashboard.
highlights: Mobile-first dashboard for tasks, habits, goals, and weekly reviews
Prisma data models for persistent application data
Reusable interface components and server-side application workflows
Deployed to a Linux production server

sections.heading: Product Design
sections.body: I designed the dashboard around everyday planning rather than one-off to-do lists: daily routines, repeat tasks, reminders, long-term goals, and an end-of-week review all live in a focused mobile-first flow.

sections.heading: Technical Build
sections.body: I designed the frontend, backend, data, and deployment architecture; implemented server-side workflows; modeled persistent data with Prisma and SQLite; and built reusable components for the core task and habit experience.

projects.title: StudyDuel
projects.shortDescription: A multiplayer quiz platform that turns study progress, profiles, and achievements into a competitive learning loop.
projects.description: StudyDuel is a team-built learning platform where custom quizzes, persistent profiles, achievements, and real-time competition reinforce one another. Across three Agile sprints, the project evolved from an early prototype into a more cohesive, authentication-aware product experience.
highlights: Core frontend developer on a 3-person team across 3 Agile sprints
Built custom quizzes, profiles, progress tracking, achievements, and account customization
Owned account customization, achievement systems, and landing-page development
Developed reusable React components and authentication-aware UI states
Integrated socket-based multiplayer features with backend APIs

sections.heading: Ownership
sections.body: As the core frontend developer, I owned account customization, the achievements system, and the landing page while contributing to the broader quiz, profile, and competitive multiplayer experience. I worked through a shared Git workflow with reviews and coordinated team tasks.

sections.heading: Interface & Integration
sections.body: I built reusable React components and connected the interface to backend APIs for persistent profiles, customization, achievements, and progress. I also helped integrate socket-based multiplayer behavior and refined user flows, visual design, and component structure.

projects.title: TSHCloud
projects.shortDescription: A long-running TrueNAS homelab for resilient storage, self-hosted services, virtualization, and remote access.
projects.description: TSHCloud is a six-drive ZFS RAIDZ2 homelab maintained for more than four years. It provides centralized storage, backups, virtual machines, secure remote access, and self-hosted services while serving as a practical environment for diagnosing infrastructure problems across the stack.
highlights: Six-drive ZFS RAIDZ2 system maintained for 4+ years
Centralized storage, backups, secure remote access, virtual machines, and self-hosted applications
Hosts photo management, file synchronization, game hosting, and application deployment
Administers datasets, SMB shares, snapshots, permissions, and persistent app storage
Troubleshoots storage, networking, virtualization, permissions, and persistence issues

sections.heading: Infrastructure
sections.body: I designed and maintained the homelab as shared infrastructure rather than a single-purpose NAS. The system supports storage and backup workflows alongside Docker-hosted applications, Linux and Windows virtual machines, and secure remote access.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.body: Day-to-day work includes managing ZFS datasets, shares, snapshots, access permissions, and persistent application storage; upgrading hosted services; and tracing failures across storage, networking, virtualization, and application state.

projects.title: Discord Music Bot
projects.shortDescription: A Node.js Discord bot for controlled music playback and queue management in voice channels.
projects.description: A JavaScript music bot that brings playback controls into Discord server voice channels. It connects Discord and YouTube APIs to handle commands, manage a queue, and limit bot features to authorized users.
highlights: Streams music into Discord voice channels
Text commands for play, pause, skip, and queue management
Access controls for bot commands and features

sections.heading: Build
sections.body: I developed the bot in Node.js, integrating the Discord and YouTube APIs to turn text commands into voice-channel playback controls. The project focused on a clear command flow, queue behavior, and permission-aware feature access.

projects.title: Minesweeper
projects.shortDescription: A C++ and SFML desktop implementation of Minesweeper with timing, leaderboards, and configurable boards.
projects.description: A desktop recreation of Minesweeper built with C++ and SFML. The project applies game-state and UI programming to deliver a playable implementation with timing, leaderboard behavior, and support for custom board dimensions.

sections.heading: Build
sections.body: I recreated the game in C++ using SFML, implementing the interactive board alongside a timer, leaderboard, and configurable board sizing. The result is a focused desktop project that combines game rules, state management, and a user-facing interface.

projects.title: 2006 BMW 330i
projects.shortDescription: An ongoing automotive diagnosis, repair, and preventative-maintenance project grounded in systems research and troubleshooting.
projects.description: A hands-on automotive project focused on improving the reliability and operating condition of a 2006 BMW 330i. Work combines diagnosis and research with repairs and preventative maintenance across electrical, sensor, drivetrain-related, fuel-injection, and routine service systems.
highlights: Diagnosed and researched sensors, alternators, transmission-related systems, and fuel-injection systems
Performed oil, fluid, gasket, tire, battery, and brake maintenance
Applied systematic troubleshooting to improve reliability and operating condition

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body: This project treats vehicle work as a technical troubleshooting practice: isolate symptoms, research likely failure points, perform repairs carefully, and use regular maintenance to prevent small issues from becoming reliability problems.
